guidance.summary: Olin forecasts third quarter 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $160 million to $200 million, with Chemical results comparable to Q2 (including an estimated $20 million impact from the Freeport VCM outage) and sequential earnings growth in Winchester.

guidance.sentence: With continued significant global volatility, third quarter 2026 adjusted EBITDA is forecast to be in the range of $160 million to $200 million,” Lane concluded.
The disruption reduced second quarter adjusted EBITDA by $40 million, with an estimated $20 million impact expected in the third quarter as full rates are planned to resume late in the quarter.

“Looking ahead, we expect our Chemical businesses’ third quarter 2026 results to be comparable to the second quarter, as reduced operating rates at the vinyl chloride monomer facility and weaker ethylene dichloride
pricing offset expected stronger caustic soda volumes.
In our Winchester business, seasonally improving commercial demand is expected to support sequential earnings growth.

In addition to the normal seasonal working capital built in first half of the year, which we expect to liquidate during the second half, Olin paid approximately $93 million, including previously accrued reserves, to resolve legacy Shintech litigation matters and expect to pay the remaining approximately $100 million in the second half of 2026.

guidance.summary: No new guidance in the window. Q3 results are due after the close on 2026-10-29, and the standing Q3 adjusted EBITDA forecast of $160-200 million is unchanged. The new credit facilities are contingent on the Huntsman merger closing.

writeup.headline: Olin rates Sell on a weak share-price trend, thin margins and flat growth, with two factors unscored.
writeup.thesis: Olin scores 32, a Sell, only 3 points above the Strong Sell line. The trend factor is the main drag at 7: the price is 45.4% below its 52-week high, 26.5% below its 200-day average, and the shares are 47.8 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days. Growth (34) is flat, with TTM revenue growth of 0.6% and a latest-quarter revenue decline of 0.9% year on year, though growth sped up by 2.8 pp from the previous quarter. Quality (42) is held back by a 6.9% gross margin and a -1.6% operating margin, and news risk (41) reflects October price-target cuts from several brokers and chlorine and caustic headwinds. Balance sheet and valuation could not be scored. On absolute terms the shares look low at a P/S of 0.3x, and they are cheap against their own history (EV/EBIT not comparable).
key_risks: Operating margin of -1.6% and negative EBIT leave little cushion if chlorine and caustic conditions stay weak.
Low cash relative to debt (cash-to-debt of 0.06) while the pending Huntsman merger and new credit facilities add complexity.
Persistent selling pressure: shares down 33.4% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago and a move from the S&P MidCap 400 to the SmallCap 600.
Q3 results due after the close on 2026-10-29 could miss the $160-200 million adjusted EBITDA forecast, with maintenance costs pushed into Q4.
Older legal matters, including the Texas emissions suit and the Shintech verdict, remain open.
what_would_change: A drop of 3 or more points, for example from further trend deterioration or more negative news, would move the rating to Strong Sell.
Reaching Hold needs 13 more points, most plausibly from a trend recovery off its very low score of 7 alongside margin improvement in quality.
Q3 results at or above the EBITDA forecast with a return to positive operating margin would lift quality and news risk.
Scored balance sheet and valuation factors could move the composite either way once their inputs are available.
